text: Persons who have previously completed or withdrawn from this study or any other investigating xanomeline TTS or the oral formulation of xanomeline.
rationale: Participation in prior xanomeline studies is not recorded in this study's data.

text: Use of any investigational agent or approved Alzheimer's therapeutic medication within 30 days prior to enrollment into the study.
rationale: CM is fully coded with start days, so approved Alzheimer's therapies are identifiable; 'any investigational agent' is not.

text: Serious illness which required hospitalization within 3 months of screening.
rationale: MH carries coded terms and dates, but neither seriousness nor hospitalisation is recorded.

text: Diagnosis of serious neurological conditions.
rationale: Nervous system conditions are identifiable by MedDRA body system; 'serious' is not defined in the data.

text: Episode of depression meeting DSM-IV criteria within 3 months of screening.
rationale: A DSM-IV determination is not recorded, and depression alone does not establish the criterion.

text: A history of mental illness within the last 5 years.
rationale: Psychiatric disorders are identifiable by body system; the specific illnesses the protocol lists are narrower than the SOC.

text: A history of syncope within the last 5 years.
rationale: Syncope would appear as a coded MH term, but 254 of 1,818 MH records are uncoded.

text: Evidence from ECG recording at screening of any listed condition.
rationale: No ECG domain is published, so no ECG finding can be evaluated. Verified absent in the data inventory.

text: A history within the last 5 years of a serious cardiovascular disorder.
rationale: Cardiac and vascular body systems are identifiable; 'serious' is not defined in the data.

text: A history within the last 5 years of a serious gastrointestinal disorder.
rationale: Gastrointestinal body system is identifiable; 'serious' is not defined in the data.

text: A history within the last 5 years of a serious endocrine disorder.
rationale: Endocrine body system is identifiable; 'serious' is not defined in the data.

text: A history within the last 5 years of a serious respiratory disorder (see list).
rationale: Respiratory body system is identifiable; the protocol's specific list is narrower than the SOC.

text: A history within the last 5 years of a serious genitourinary disorder.
rationale: Renal and urinary body system is identifiable; 'serious' is not defined in the data.

text: A history within the last 5 years of a serious rheumatologic disorder.
rationale: Musculoskeletal body system is identifiable; 'serious' is not defined in the data.

text: A known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) within the last 5 years.
rationale: HIV would appear as a coded MH term; absence of a term is weaker evidence than a negative test.

text: A history within the last 5 years of a serious infectious disease (see list in protocol).
rationale: Infections body system is identifiable; the protocol's list of serious infections is narrower.

text: A history within the last 5 years of a primary or recurrent malignant disease (with exceptions, see list in protocol).
rationale: Neoplasms body system is identifiable; the protocol's carve-outs are not encoded.

text: Visual, hearing, or communication disabilities impairing the ability to participate in the study; (for example, inability to speak or understand English, illiteracy).
rationale: Visual, hearing and communication disabilities are not collected.

text: Laboratory test values exceeding the Lilly Reference Range III for the patient's age in any of the following analytes: creatinine, total bilirubin, SGOT, SGPT, etc.
rationale: Every named analyte is in LB with a reference range, but the protocol's Lilly Reference Range III is proprietary and unavailable; the study's own range is a documented proxy.

text: Central laboratory test values below reference range for folate, and vitamin B12, and outside reference range for thyroid function tests.
rationale: Vitamin B12 and TSH are in LB; folate, total T4, thyroid uptake and the free thyroid index are not published.

text: Positive syphilis screening with confirmatory testing.
rationale: No syphilis test is among the 43 analytes in LB.

text: Central laboratory test value above reference range for glycosylated hemoglobin (A1C) (insulin dependent diabetes mellitus patients only).
rationale: HbA1c is in LB and the 9.5% threshold is in the protocol, but the criterion applies only to insulin-dependent diabetics, which the data does not reliably identify.

text: Treatment with medications within 1 month prior to enrollment (see list).
rationale: CM carries an ATC-style class and start day, but the protocol's 19-class washout table maps imperfectly and some records are UNCODED.

text: Males and postmenopausal females at least 50 years of age.
rationale: Age is in DM.AGE and checkable. Postmenopausal status is not collected anywhere, so the sex clause cannot be evaluated.

text: Diagnosis of probable AD as defined by NINCDS and the ADRDA guidelines (Protocol Attachment LZZT.7).
rationale: MH records a PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS for every randomized subject, but the NINCDS-ADRDA determination behind it is not recorded.

text: MMSE score of 10 to 23.
rationale: MMSE items are in QS; the total is derived by summing them and reproduces the range and mean printed in the CSR.

text: Modified Hachinski Ischemic Scale score of <= 4. (Protocol Attachment LZZT.8).
rationale: All 13 Modified Hachinski items are in QS and sum to the published scale maximum.

text: CNS imaging (CT scan or MRI of brain) compatible with AD within past 1 year.
rationale: No imaging domain is published, so CNS imaging compatibility cannot be evaluated.

text: Investigator has obtained informed consent signed by the patient (and/or legal representative) and by the caregiver.
rationale: DM.RFICDTC shows a consent date exists; whether the document was signed by patient and caregiver is not recorded.

text: Geographic proximity to investigator's site that allows adequate follow-up.
rationale: Geographic proximity to the site is not collected.

text: Caregiverwill monitor administration of prescribed medications, and will be responsible for the overall care of the patient at home.
rationale: Caregiver reliability and willingness are not collected.
